title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
read_level: full (v1 PDF main text, tables I-IX, limitations; appendix tables X-XI skimmed)
why_wsp: A local LLM (Ollama gemma4) proposes structured JSON edits (stage/channel scaling, low-rank, head edits) to pretrained YOLO26 weights, scored by forward evaluation on COCO; compared against random, DE, CMA-ES and a matched random-policy hybrid.
editor: local Ollama model identified in logs as gemma4:latest; plus non-LLM optimizers (random search, differential evolution, CMA-ES, TPE) and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES
interface: other (schema-validated JSON edit actions: scaling, perturbation, low-rank, head, sparsification, interpolation; or CMA-ES over LLM-chosen subspace)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (LLM reads evaluation history and failure diagnostics; search budgets B = 8 to 250)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Edit size bounded rather than counted: "a 1% nominal relative norm ceiling for expanded actions" (Sec. IV-B)

headline_results.claim: Larger CMA-ES budget raises dev gain but not selection
headline_results.quote: increasing CMA-ES evaluations from 8 to 250 improved mean development gains from +0.11 to +0.28 percentage points, while the corresponding selection changes remained negative (from -0.03 to -0.12 points)

headline_results.claim: LLM hybrid vs matched random-policy hybrid
headline_results.where: Table VII (also B=25 p=0.369, B=50 p=0.694)

headline_results.quote: the mean official COCO AP change was +0.004 points with a reported 95% interval [−0.026, +0.034]

headline_results.claim: Phase II TPE-selected champion on holdout
headline_results.quote: Observed paired change +0.0580 pp Bootstrap 95% interval [-0.026, +0.123] pp

headline_results.claim: Real LLM dev gains smaller than DE/CMA-ES at budget 15
headline_results.quote: DE and CMA-ES reached approximately +0.13 and +0.12 points, while real LLM methods produced smaller positive changes (approximately +0.03 to +0.06 points)
Under the final strict schema, 53 are accepted and 172 rejected.

cost.quote: the real LLM-feedback method consumed 36,469 reported tokens over the experiment group

cost.where: Table V (mean time in s, B=250 CMA-ES)

baselines_and_controls: Unchanged checkpoint; deterministic scaling; random Gaussian perturbation; random search; differential evolution; CMA-ES; TPE/Bayesian; matched random-policy hybrid (same CMA-ES and bounds, no semantic context); an earlier Gaussian 'LLMGuidedOptimizer' simulator retained as a control.
runs_and_variance: Budget-dependent seeds: "five seeds at B = 8 and 25 for major numerical methods, three at B = 50, two at B = 100, and one at B = 250" (Sec. IV-D); paired t-tests with 95% CI; image-level paired bootstrap; YOLO26m five seeds.
robustness_of_edits: Transfer to disjoint selection set tested: gains largely do not transfer; cross-capacity transfer "A transferred small-model editing policy was not reliably beneficial on larger models" (Sec. X-A).
verification: statistical only (paired t-tests, bootstrap CIs); schema validation of actions; immutable-checkpoint and gradient checks in software package
memorization_vs_reasoning: Matched random-policy hybrid shows no demonstrated LLM advantage: "interpretability of a proposal is different from predictive utility of the proposal" (Sec. XII-B).
limitations_stated: Fresh partition has contradictory Train2017/Val2017 lineage; selection partition reused across phases; native vs COCO API metric differences; Phase V narrative and packaged table disagree; budgets 100/250 have 2/1 seeds; retrospective schema check cannot prove historic tensor execution (Sec. XII-E).
code_or_data: none found (paper refers to an accompanying project archive; no URL given)
notes_for_survey: Careful negative/null-result evaluation of LLM-guided gradient-free weight editing on a vision detector, with a matched random-policy control and explicit disclosure of evaluation-set reuse and an earlier mislabeled Gaussian 'LLM' simulator. Does not cite the Takehi et al. blog explicitly, though it uses the term weight-space programming in index terms and Fig. 1.
